Sustainable Development Fee: YouLi lists "Government tax" as included. Is the SDF inside the $4,500 starting price, or shown as its own line like on Brian's Bhutan pages?
Overnights for days 4–6 and the trek are not stated. Punakha and Khotokha hotels? Camping on the trek?

seo.title: Bhutan Adventure: Central and Western Bhutan | Adventure Access
seo.description: A week to ten days in Bhutan: Thimphu, Punakha, your choice of rafting, biking, birding or hiking, and the Tiger's Nest. From $4,500.

hero.title: Bhutan

intro.label: The Journey
intro.heading: Bhutan, Your Way
paragraphs: Bhutan is a place of old forests, clear rivers, snow-capped peaks and warm subtropical valleys. This Buddhist kingdom is one of the least visited countries in the world, yet it has some of the best hiking, biking, rafting and cultural immersion in the Himalaya.

This journey pairs Bhutan's history, culture and food with activities chosen to fit your appetite for adventure. The middle of the trip is yours to shape, and a multi-day trek can stretch it to ten days.

dayTypes.label: How the Days Work
dayTypes.heading: Set Days, Your Days
dayTypes.lede: The start and finish are set: the capital, Punakha and Paro. The middle is built around the adventures you choose, and your guide adjusts it on the ground.

cards.title: Culture days
cards.body: Days 1–3 and 10: Thimphu's dzong, museum and Takin Preserve, Punakha Dzong over Dochu La, and Paro to finish.

cards.title: Your adventure days
cards.body: Days 4–6 in Punakha and Khotokha: rafting, mountain biking, birding or hiking. Mix them, or go deeper on one.

cards.title: Optional trek
cards.body: Days 7–9: a multi-day hike, such as sections of the Trans Bhutan Trail, with a hand-picked trekking crew.

chapters.label: The Journey in Chapters
chapters.heading: From the Capital to the Tiger's Nest

groups.title: Thimphu — Into the Capital (7,656 ft)

image.alt: Prayer flags above the Thimphu valley

prose: Approaching Bhutan is like nothing else. The Himalaya fill the horizon, and your first Bhutanese hosts are on the plane, since only the national airlines fly in and out. Paro is just the port of entry for now; you will see the best of it at the end.

days.label: Day 1
days.text: Land in Paro (7,200 ft), a quick meal, then about an hour's drive to Thimphu. An easy afternoon to adjust to the altitude, and dinner with the group and a full orientation from your guides.

days.label: Day 2
days.text: A walking day in the capital at an acclimatizing pace: a dzong, a cultural museum and the Takin Preserve, for a first look at Bhutan's Buddhist culture, history and wildlife.

groups.title: Punakha via Dochu La
prose: The road crosses Dochu La, with views of Bhutan's great peaks from the top, then drops into Punakha. Its riverside dzong was built in 1637, saw the coronation of the first king in 1907, and was the capital until 1955.

days.label: Day 3
days.text: Over Dochu La to Punakha. Wander the dzong while your guide explains its many roles, then a night near Punakha before your adventure days.

groups.title: Punakha and Khotokha — Your Adventure Days

image.alt: A long suspension bridge over a river in Punakha

prose: Punakha is an adventurer's dream. These three days are shaped around what you choose: several activities, or more time on one.

days.label: Rafting
days.text: A relaxed float on the Mo Chhu, or faster water and bigger rapids on the Pho Chhu.

days.label: Biking
days.text: Mountain biking in Khotokha's quiet valley.

days.label: Birding
days.text: The region's Ramsar wetland, with a chance of black-necked cranes in season.

days.label: Hiking
days.text: A hike to one of the region's cultural or spiritual landmarks.

groups.title: Optional Multi-Day Trek

image.alt: Three hikers under a traditional gate on the trail

prose: Once you are adjusted to the altitude, pick one of Bhutan's famous trails for a longer hike. The Trans Bhutan Trail is one option: string several sections together with a trekking crew hand-picked for their skill and personality.

days.label: Days 7–9
days.text: A multi-day hike in central or western Bhutan, matched to your fitness and the rest of your itinerary.

groups.title: Paro and the Tiger's Nest

image.alt: The Tiger's Nest monastery on its cliff

prose: Back to where it began. The Tiger's Nest can only be reached on foot, and the hike is the best way to end any trip to Bhutan: activity, culture and mountainside forest in one day.

days.label: Day 10
days.text: Walk Paro's streets, try Bhutan's home-grown coffee, and shop for something to remember the trip by. Hike to the Tiger's Nest, then a traditional hot stone bath at a family farmhouse.

days.label: Day 11
days.text: Your guide takes you to Paro airport for your flight home.

highlights.title: Taktsang — Tiger's Nest
highlights.body: Bhutan's most iconic monastery, reachable only on foot, and the finale of the trip.

highlights.title: Punakha Dzong
highlights.body: Built in 1637, site of the first king's coronation in 1907 and Bhutan's capital until 1955.

highlights.title: The Trans Bhutan Trail
highlights.body: Add a multi-day trek on Bhutan's famous trails with a hand-picked trekking crew, matched to your fitness.

goodToKnow.label: Good to Know
goodToKnow.heading: Before You Go
goodToKnow.lede: A few things that shape how this trip runs.

cards.title: Getting there
cards.body: Only Bhutan's national airlines fly into Paro, the country's one international airport. Flights to and from Bhutan are not included.

cards.title: Altitude
cards.body: Paro sits at 7,200 feet and Thimphu at 7,656 feet. The first days are paced to help you adjust before the adventure days.

cards.title: Your guides
cards.body: Professional English-speaking guides travel with you, with specialist guides for each activity.

cards.title: Black-necked cranes
cards.body: Crane sightings around the Ramsar wetland are seasonal. Ask us when to go if they matter to you.

stays.label: Where You'll Stay
stays.heading: Hotels and a Farmhouse
paragraphs: Our preferred packages use 3–4 star hotels. In Paro we always recommend a family farmhouse, some dating back seven generations. Farmhouses are not rated like hotels, but every guest names them as a highlight.

notes: Ask us for a price for your dates, group and chosen activities.

included: Professional English-speaking guides and activity guides
Activities as listed in your itinerary
Accommodations: 3–4 star hotels and a farmhouse stay
All ground transportation by private vehicle
excluded: Alcohol (we strongly encourage little or none while acclimatizing)
Tips for guides (we will explain local tipping customs)
Personal clothing and equipment (we send a packing list)
